package_info.package_versions: All versions found in malicious repositories (e.g., main.py, hackingtool.py, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains obfuscated code that, when executed, steals sensitive information such as passwords, browser cookies, Discord tokens, and other PC information, and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled server. The code is intentionally hidden and embedded in fake or trojanized open-source projects to trick users into executing it.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (as soon as the file is executed or imported)
execution_context.file_location: main.py, hackingtool.py, or similar entry-point Python files

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code decodes a base64-encoded payload, compiles it, and executes it in memory, enabling arbitrary code execution that can access files, environment variables, and perform network exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of dynamic code execution via exec and compile, combined with base64 decoding, is a classic obfuscation and payload delivery technique used to hide malicious intent and bypass static analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Python packages do not execute obfuscated, dynamically-decoded code at import or runtime, especially not in entry-point files. Legitimate packages should not hide their logic or perform arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic code execution may be used in advanced plugin systems or for loading user-supplied scripts in controlled environments, but never for hidden payloads in open-source tools.
key_indicators: Appears in entry-point files of suspicious projects

attack_chain.action: User downloads and executes or imports the malicious Python file (e.g., main.py, hackingtool.py) from a fake or trojanized repository.
Obfuscated code is decoded, compiled, and executed in memory, granting the attacker full control to steal sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft and exfiltration to attacker-controlled server

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic execution of base64-decoded payloads using exec/compile
Immediate network connections after import or execution
Access to sensitive files (browser data, Discord tokens, etc.)
file_indicators: Obfuscated or padded code blocks in main.py, hackingtool.py, or similar files
Unusually long lines with excessive whitespace
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled C2 servers (often hardcoded in the decoded payload)
Exfiltration of data via HTTP/S POST requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Python files for the use of __import__('builtins').exec and base64 decoding patterns, especially in entry-point scripts. Flag any code that decodes and executes base64-encoded payloads at import or runtime. Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections immediately after running such scripts, and look for access to sensitive files or environment variables. Pay special attention to projects with suspicious names targeting automation for Discord, TikTok, or similar platforms.
